editorial:
Imagine you are living in 1939 Germany and your only way to survive is a ticket on a big ship. You get to board the St. Louis with hundreds of other Jewish families, feeling like you finally found a way out of the Nazi nightmare. The vibe starts with a spark of hope as the passengers celebrate their freedom on the open sea, thinking Cuba is their safe harbor. You will feel the tension build as the movie shows the contrast between the luxury of the ship and the scary reality waiting for them on land.

What really works here is how the movie makes you feel the desperation of the passengers. The acting is solid and the slow build-up of dread keeps you glued to the screen. While it is a heavy story that can be hard to watch, it is an important piece of history. It is a great pick for a family discussion about history.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a heartbreaking note when Cuba refuses to let the passengers land. After floating near the coast for days, the ship is forced to head back to Europe. Some families are lucky enough to find homes in the US or Canada, but many others are sent back to Germany. You learn that many of those people ended up dying in the Holocaust, showing that their hope for safety was stolen by politics.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories and history.
